profile_text.body:
Databricks, founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, describes itself as a unified data and AI platform for enterprises. The company's site says its platform handles analytical and operational workloads on a single open, governed foundation, covering ETL, data warehousing, streaming, business intelligence, and AI application development. Key offerings include Lakebase, which the company describes as merging Postgres-style transactional reliability with data lakehouse scale and governance, and Databricks Genie, a conversational analytics interface that lets business users query enterprise data in plain language without SQL or coding.

On the AI side, Databricks tracks two closely related products: DBRX, an open-source large language model built on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture intended for enterprise training and deployment, and the broader Databricks AI platform, which incorporates DBRX alongside MLflow for model governance and Unity Catalog for data governance and lineage tracking. The site also describes Unity Gateway as a multi-AI governance and cost control layer for managing access, spend, and observability across agents, models, and tools from a single interface.

The held facts show 161 legal matters with California exposure on record, though no specific cases are detailed in the available data. Databricks operates as a for-profit startup and maintains a presence on theworldofai.org under its own profile page.
